title: CDC: About PLACES: Local Data for Better Health
quote: Local health problems and priority health risk behaviors for action.
claim: CDC identifies local health problems and priorities as a use of PLACES. This does not establish use of Fieldwork.

title: CDC: Frequently Asked Questions — Using the Data
quote: Identify the health issues facing a local area or neighborhoods.
claim: CDC describes neighborhood health issue identification as an intended use; its caveats also prohibit evaluating local interventions using these estimates alone.

title: WSFA: Montgomery seeks blight ordinance for dilapidated buildings
quote: give the city more flexibility to address the dozens of vacant, dilapidated homes and commercial buildings across the city.
claim: Original reporting documents a local council discussion about vacant and dilapidated properties. Historical reporting, not a claim about current law.

title: Greenlund et al.: PLACES: Local Data for Better Health
quote: Effective planning and decision making rely on credible health information.
claim: The original methods paper explains the local information gap and planning need; this is not evidence of Fieldwork use.

title: Carlson et al.: Linking Local-Level Chronic Disease and Social Vulnerability Measures to Inform Planning Efforts: A COPD Example
quote: Examples of how to combine and use data across different sources are lacking.
claim: The original study identifies a gap in cross-source analysis examples and demonstrates joining health and vulnerability data; it does not prove an association between Montgomery code enforcement and health.
